text:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we move coarse-grained RBAC checks to the dashboard ingress (query gateway) and keep fine-grained enforcement in the query executor. Goal is to reduce backend work and improve p95 when panels are crawled by dashboards.

sam: Sounds sensible. Can you sketch the failure modes? My worry is double-checking consistency and leakage with row-level perms.

maya: Yep. Failure modes: 1) stale auth cache at ingress -> over-allow until executor blocks (low blast, but extra work). 2) ingress false-deny -> user sees missing panels (bad UX). 3) cache key explosion if we bind too many perm-attrs.

lee: How about a hybrid: gateway does tenant/scoped-channel filtering (coarse) and returns a permission-hash header. Executor validates the hash against row-level rules for each response. That keeps most cheap rejects at edge and guarantees correctness in executor.

olivia: Important note: any permission-hash must be derived from stable attributes only: role, tenant-id, feature-flags. Avoid ephemeral attributes (session_id, last-active). Otherwise cache churn kills gains.

sam: Agree with olivia. Also: caching strategy for panel-level results needs a key of (query-signature, permission-hash, time-bucket). Otherwise a national cache will leak across roles.

maya: Exactly. Example key: `panel_v1|qsig:SHA256(...)|perm:sha1(role:viewer,tenant:42)|t:60s`. Keeps TTL short for interactive dashboards.

olivia: How do we handle datasets with row-level filters that depend on query inputs (date range)? Many panels pass arbitrary filters and the gateway won't know them all.

lee: We only pre-filter on attributes that are independent of the ad-hoc query (tenant, org role). For anything query-dependent, the executor must still evaluate. The ingress can still short-circuit some common known patterns (e.g., tenant-id in path).

maya: Tradeoffs listed in bullet form:
- Pros: reduces executor CPU on common fast rejects, better cache hit rate for same-perm users, lower p95 for panel render.
- Cons: increased complexity, potential UX inconsistency, cache-key cardinality risk.

sam: Operational ask: what metrics do we add to validate? I propose: `auth.gateway.requests`, `auth.gateway.false_denies`, `panel.cache.hit_rate_by_perm`, `panel.exec.validation_latency`, and a `leakage_alert` counter for cross-perm hits.

olivia: Also add `missing-panel-rate` per-dashboard to catch ingress false-denies. We should surface top 10 affected dashboards in the console.

lee: Rollout plan suggestion:
1) telemetry-only mode — gateway computes permission-hash header and logs decision but returns normal flow. 2) cache-key pilot for a small set of low-risk dashboards (internal support dashboards). 3) enable pre-filter for 5% of users (canary) with an auto-disable if `missing-panel-rate` spikes >1% relative. 4) ramp 5% -> 25% -> 100% with checks.

maya: Canary config snippet (deploy-bot):
``` 
# ingress config
rbac:
  mode: telemetry | prefilter
  perm_attrs: [tenant_id, role]
  canary_pct: 5
  missing_panel_threshold: 0.01
  emit_headers: [x-perm-hash]
```
deploy-bot: Canary template created in `infra/deploys/ingress/rbac-prefilter.yaml` and linked to the canary pipeline. Will create the telemetry dashboard for the metrics mentioned. :robot_face:

sam: Performance knobs: keep TTLs small (30-120s) for interactive panels. Consider a small LRU per-ingress node for perm-hash->deny decisions to avoid repeated expensive lookups.

olivia: Security note: the permission-hash header must be signed by ingress key and validated by executor to avoid spoofing. Also ensure no raw perms are included in logs/headers in prod.

maya: Action items:
- lee: implement permission-hash generator and header contract (PR by EOD Wednesday).
- sam: add telemetry panels and leakage alerts (PR for dashboards).
- olivia: threat model review and header signing plan.
- maya: draft rollout page for SRE runbook + rollback triggers.

lee: I'll start the generator. One more question: should we version the header name? I vote `x-rd-perm-v1` so we can change algorithm later.

maya: +1 for versioning. Use `x-rd-perm-v1`.

sam: SGTM. Happy to pair on metrics.

olivia: I'll schedule a quick 30m sync after PRs land to validate instrumentation.

maya: Thanks team — will post the follow-up RFC note with the config and the canary playbook. :thumbsup:
